prompt:
Use your built-in image generation tool to create exactly ONE image for a video game art pipeline. Do not run shell commands, do not write or edit files and do not ask questions. When the image exists, reply only with the word DONE.

Style: a flat orthographic product illustration of a luxurious vintage-inspired Eurorack synthesizer module in the spirit of a harmonium or pipe-organ console: deep warm ebony-brown anodised panel, polished brass and ivory details, fine engraved double hairline brass borders, art-deco arches and notched corners, music-staff line ornaments, subtle realistic metal shading on knobs, buttons and jacks only. Palette: ebony #1B1613, walnut #2A1F1A, oxblood #4A1D2A, brass #C8A24A, bright brass #EBD08A, ivory #F2E8D0, verdigris #3F9C8F. Avoid blue panels, avoid neon, avoid cold greys.

Subject: the complete front panel of a wide Eurorack module, 42 HP wide (213 mm) and 128.5 mm tall, seen perfectly straight on, landscape orientation, the panel filling the whole image with no rack, no wall and no hands around it. Left: a recessed jack field with rows of round black jacks with brass nut rings and tiny glowing amber LEDs, divided by thin brass lines. Centre: two large brass-capped knobs with ivory pointers at the top, a small dark display screen with a warm amber glowing line of note shapes, four more brass knobs below, and a small grid of round ivory buttons. Right: five bordered sections framed with double hairline brass rules, each with a brass arch-shaped header cartouche (blank, no letters) and grids of round ivory buttons with brass bezels, each button with a small coloured ring, one of eight harmonic colours (gold, rose, verdigris, violet, sky blue, moss green, orange, pearl) according to its row; a few brass knobs. Decorative five-line music staff ornaments between sections. No letters visible; all labels are tiny blank shapes.

The artwork fills the entire frame, with no frame, border, wall, easel or hands around it.

Strictly no text, letters, numbers, words, lettering, logos, brand marks, watermarks or signatures. No real people or celebrities, no real brands, no real-world landmarks.
